messages.subject: fit negative binomial in mediation path models
messages.subject_clean: fit negative binomial in mediation path models
messages.body_plain:
Hi blavaan community,

How can blavaan fit negative binomial instead of regular regression for mediation path models? My outcome measure is highly (positively) skewed. Since FIML cannot be used for binary options (if dichotomized) in lavaan, I am trying to figure out if I can use highly skewed outcome measures as they are.

Terrence D. Jorgensen wrote "Bayesian lavaan package will write a JAGS script (the Bayesian software that actually fits the model), which you can adjust to add the appropriate link function and likelihood function for the data." But I am not sure how to do that. I would really appreciate your answer.

Here is my model using lavaan:

p16a18c24 <- '
# direct effect
myOutcome ~ c*myPredictor
# mediator
myMediator1 ~ a1*myPredictor
myOutcome ~ b1*myMediator1
myMediator2 ~ a2*myPredictor
myOutcome ~ b2*myMediator2
myMediator3 ~ a3*myPredictor
myOutcome ~ b3*myMediator3
# variances: any variable that was listed as DV
myOutcome ~~ myOutcome
myMediator1 ~~ myMediator1
myMediator2 ~~ myMediator2
myMediator3 ~~ myMediator3
# covariances: mediators who are (positively) correlated with each other
myMediator1 ~~ myMediator2
myMediator2 ~~ myMediator3
myMediator3 ~~ myMediator1
# intercepts: *1, only for DVs
myOutcome ~ 1
myMediator1 ~ 1
myMediator2 ~ 1
myMediator3 ~ 1
# indirect effects (a*b)
ab1 := a1*b1
ab2 := a2*b2
ab3 := a3*b3
# total effect
total := c + (a1*b1) + (a2*b2) + (a3*b3)
'
fit.p16a18c24 <- sem(p16a18c24,data=m,missing="fiml",se="bootstrap")
summary(fit.p16a18c24,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE,rsquare=TRUE)

Thanks in advance,
NewInMediation

messages.body_plain:
NewInMediation,

It is possible to fit this model, but it might require more coding and expertise than desired. Basically, you would use a command like

fit <- bsem(p16a18c24,data=m, jagfile=TRUE, do.fit=FALSE)

This will write a file called "sem.jag" to the lavExport folder. You would have to open that file, modify it (replacing some dnorm()'s with dnbinom()), then re-run it with the run.jags() command. For more detail, see the "Extensions of JAGS syntax" section of my paper here:

https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.05604.pdf

You would also have to compute fit metrics on your own, because blavaan only handles normal distributions here. (This is actually a tough problem because the fit measures integrate out the latent variables, and we need integral approximation if the distributions are not normal.)

Ed

Dear group,

I found a discrepancy between the model syntaxes used by lavaan and blavaan.
When specifying a multiple mediators model in lavaan I use to recycle the parameters defined by the ':=' operator.
For example:
indirectEffect := a*b
total := c + (a*b)

indirectEffect := a*b

Anyway, blavaan and lavaan are great and thank you guys for creating, developing, and making them available to us.

Sanne,

In jags, it can be helpful to jointly put an inverse wishart on variance/covariance parameters associated with latent variables. However, when you start to put custom priors on latent variable parameters, it can become impossible to use an inverse wishart. So blavaan checks whether you are using your own custom priors on latent variable parameters, then decides what to do about this prior.

The blavaan paper has lots of detail on custom specification of these priors. Basically, if you don't use an inverse wishart, you can write each covariance as the product of a correlation and two standard deviations. Then the priors go on the correlation (beta) and associated variances (inverse gamma).

Either of these specifications (inverse wishart or correlation/variances) is valid. The sampling under inverse wishart might be a little more efficient, but it will not make a major difference in many situations.

Best,
Ed

Sonja,

In the blavaan paper (url below), there is an "extensions of jags syntax" section that shows how to modify the underlying jags code.

I think you would start by not changing the priors in your model, then export jags code, then find the part that assigns a wishart prior (part of the line will look like " ~ dwish(iden, 3)"). Then change the wishart parameters.

dp = dpriors(ibpsi="dwish(iden,10)")

Finally, if you are looking to match default mplus priors, you won't be able to do it because jags does not allow for improper priors (like gamma or wishart distributions with negative parameters).

Ed

If you could send data from your model with "satisfaction =~ 1*satis", that would be helpful. It seems like you might obtain the same model by treating satis as manifest, but I'm not certain.

Also, ppp is the only metric built in to blavaan for judging absolute model fit. The other metrics are used for model comparison.

Ed

Rémi,

Thanks for the code/data. I just took a look at this, and I think all your models should work in the development version of blavaan (and still not sure why you are having problems with that).

I agree that your model with residual covariances seems to have decent fit. It might be a challenge to justify the residual covariances if you only added them when the original model did not fit well. Ideally, you would be able to show that this model also has a good fit in new data (that were not used to build the original model).

Best,
Ed

Ed
